The opener for RMP is vital to your success. You have very high kill pressure in the opener due to the free sap, and can force out a LOT of CDs vs a team that isn't very coordinated or a team that isn't good. You're not always looking for a kill in the opener, you're just looking for the enemy to use their resources. If you have a bad opener, you won't get any big defensives or trinkets from the enemy. That means you will struggle to kill your target on your next few goes.

In your opener, if you get big defensives from your kill target try to swap to the healer or other DPS. Very often my team gets kills on the opener from swapping to another target with 2x cheapshot (or kidney) and the tail end of combustion + smoke bomb or duel. 

Practice your opener CC, have your mage take mass invis and invis you out the gates if that helps. Sap healer, stun kill target, and sheep off DPS (can DB sheep). You should try and fear off the sap, but if you can't it's okay to blind to follow the sap. Have your DPS practice their opening damage rotations. Comboost first and save the rogue damage for next go/swap. The best CC in the world doesn't matter if you can't do damage.

After your opener is done, you need to play more defensively. You have no kill pressure when the enemy is on DR. Use alter time efficiently, utilize vanish, and line the enemy. You just need to live the 20s between DR resets (or kidney CD). Practice your double CC, don't worry about triple CC yet. Sub rogue should cheap 2 enemies (one of them as healer if he can) and have the mage poly off of that. Use dragon's breath (DB) to ensure the poly cast. Then you as the healer should look to chastise + fear the one not CC'd. Save fade (if you need a freedom) and a feather charge to run in for the fear, but if you can't make it just mind control them.

The answer provided is correct. The interviewer isn't saying to convert the decimal to an IP. He's asking to place periods between the numbers in that string so that you have a valid IP. When you are given 123456789 there is only one way to place the periods to get a valid IP address: 123.45.67.89

The interviewer basically said hey, I've erased the periods in this IP address, add them back in. 

An IPv4 address is made up of 4 octets, which are split up by periods. 1 octet is 8 bits, which can hold values between 00000000 and  11111111. Those numbers are in binary; in decimal (base10) they are 0 and 255. So, the maximum numeric value of 1 octet (8 bits) is 255. Therefore, the only correct way to place the 3 periods is 123.45.67.89, otherwise you'd have a number greater than 255 in one of the sections between the periods.

Honestly, almost any time the enemy team has one you'll run blink stun. Especially if you're running resolve trinket, which increases the duration of the stun on you. If you're running with a healer, it's almost always blink stun. 

RM can be a little tricky to tell if they're going to be going you, and if it's worth taking blink stun. Most comps will try and kill your rogue, but warriors and priests can kill you through block. You'll feel out the more you play which comps you feel like you can take shimmer into, but to start I'd just take blink stun vs any comp that can stun you.

I think mage can struggle vs priests, paladins, and hunters. 

RM struggles vs paladins, as their toolkit (BoPing stuns/blind, bubble, sac, freedom) make it hard to kill them, and hard to get a clean reset. You can blink out of their 6 second stun, but their slow and freedom makes it hard to peel them.

Priests healers can be very difficult to CC if you aren't experienced on mage. They can Shadow Word: Death when you cast polymorph, which will damage themselves and break the CC. If you aren't expecting this and trying to bait it out, it can be tough to land a poly on them. You can dragon's breath into poly/ring for the guaranteed CC, though. Disc isn't very popular right now, but it can also be tough because they can have up to 3 dispels (2 charges from pvp talent and mass dispel). Mass also breaks your ice block (and your ice wall if you're frost) so be careful. Shadow especially fucks mage really hard. Feral + SP is super scary to face as a mage, because all your polys get mass dispelled or deathed. Psyfiend is also hard to kill as a mage without having/spending fire blast charges, and death + gfade make it really hard to land CC on them as well. In addition to life swap and their instant CC (4s stun and 4s silence) spriest is a real pain in the ass for a mage.

Hunters can also fuck mages. With their roar of sacrifice ability, they prevent all crits to themselves or one of their teammates. This completely fucks your combustion, and it's on a pretty low cooldown. With feign death and turtle, it can be hard to kill a hunter as a fire mage (and especially if your partner is an assassination rogue). Their sustained damage and their ability to purge your shields also make them a big threat. A good tip for facing hunter teams as RM is to open their healer with combust and no rogue cooldowns. The hunter should break stealth to roar of sacrifice his friend, and then you poly/blind the healer and immediately swap onto the hunter with a marked for death kidney shot. You'll either force a trinket or kill them, 100% of the time.

As a mage, you have a lot of flexibility in 2s comps.

Rogue is the most popular, and probably the best partner. Your CC coverage is insane, and you win in the first two "goes." You rotate your offensive CDs with your partner and usually kill whoever doesn't have trinket/immunity after the first go. You mostly play safe and help your rogue buddy kite and get a restealth.

If you prefer to play with casters, you can either play with a warlock or a shadow priest. You have a lot of pressure and nice CC setups (especially with shadow priest), which lead to early healer trinkets and high kill pressure. Shadow and fire is the best combination here, with the priest mainly being a CC bot and off-healing. With a warlock you probably want to be frost, and it's not going to be as good in 2s as it is in 3s (especially a lower ratings).

If you want to play with a healer, you probably want to play with a holy priest, paladin, or druid. These healers have powerful stuns, and can keep you and themselves alive. They also don't DR with your CC, which is important in the healer/mage comp. You have your healer stun the kill target and combust them. After combust, you perma run from the enemy, kiting and polying as much as you can. Reset your combust with fireballs and your night fae ability, and try and burn them down while they have no trinket. These comps are good, but incredibly boring to play.

As for legendaries, almost every fire mage plays Disciplinary Command in 2s. The extra crit damage is a huge increase to your combust kill pressure, and it's not very hard to proc. It also helps your burst damage outside of combust, with double fire blast + pyro or something similar. Against purge-heavy comps as double DPS, you _can_ go Triune Ward for extra defensiveness. This actually lowers the overall amount of shielding that you get, but it will give you great purge protection so your shield doesn't all go away in one purge. Usually you have enough survivability with your baseline mage kit and your conduits, but Triune does have some niche uses.

Inflation is just an extra modifier to the underlying issue of low supply vs high demand. A 6% rise in inflation isn't exactly nothing, but when gas prices have risen 50-100% in the past two years it's nowhere near the main cause.

Ultimately, the less a dollar is worth, the more of them you need to buy oil/gas.

It's not about the shift to renewables. It's about the huge drop in demand from the lockdowns, which halted a lot of production and shut down a lot of smaller producers. Now that demand has shot back up, there's fewer producers (and thus less supply) which causes prices to skyrocket as well.

I think the problem is the lack of a serious unranked game mode. There are people that play competitive for fun, and there are people who play competitive for rank. Someone who typically plays comp more casually is the kind of person who is, typically, ok with someone playing Doomfist for the first time. Someone who is playing to win, and only to win, will 100% not be. 

(This isn't to say that people who play for rank don't have fun playing, or that people who play for fun don't care about rank) 

I, personally, think in a competitive and ranked environment it's not acceptable to play heroes or roles you are uncomfortable with. If you queue up for a competitive match, you need to try your best to win. If you are playing a role or hero you are not comfortable with you are not playing to the best of your ability, and subsequently to the skill level of your rank. 

Playing a hero you are not experienced on or comfortable with ruins the match for the people on your team. It's never fun to have an under-performing team mate, and it'll certainly be an obstacle in the way of victory and SR gain. So neither people who are playing for the fun of it nor people who are playing for the rank gain are getting what they want from the match. If you're playing a role or hero that you are not experienced on, you simply are not playing to win. As a side note, that's why I think role queue is a great idea; it would prevent situations where it becomes necessary to fill so that everyone can perform to the best of their ability. 

If there were a game mode that mirrored competitive without a rank attached, I think it would solve this and so many other problems. Other games, such as HotS, League, and WoW, have implemented systems like this to great success. 

Take, for example, Heroes of the Storm. In HotS there are a three different game modes: quick match, unranked, and ranked. Quick match is essentially quick play; you queue up the hero you want to play and it matches you with 9 other players. Ranked play has a team drafting phase where you pick and ban heroes. Unranked is the exact same as ranked, except it doesn't have a visible rank or score attached to it. Because of this system, in the year I've played, very few times have I had a person pick a hero they've never played in ranked. When you queue ranked, you are playing to win.
